Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helios is excited to move the pilot forward. Attached are our redlines to the pricing exhibit (Helios_redlines_v2.docx). High-level asks:

- For the 90-day pilot, can we waive the floor (minimum commit) for month 1 and cap only at 3x the pilot consumption? We need a softer entry for proof-of-value.

Avery / team —

Quick legal-comments and suggested clause edits below. I'm keeping this focused on operational language so procurement can sign without restating core commercial terms.

1) Pilot floor waiver (month 1). Suggested language: "Notwithstanding Section X (Minimum Monthly Commitment), for the initial 30-day pilot period (the "Pilot"), Customer's minimum monthly commitment shall be set to zero for the first calendar month of the Pilot. The Pilot shall otherwise be subject to the charges set forth in the Order Schedule."

Rationale: explicit waiver avoids ambiguity.

2) Cap behavior. Two options:
  a) Billing Cap: "During the Pilot, Redwood's invoiced charges for usage shall not exceed three (3) times the estimated Pilot consumption as set forth in the Order Schedule. Usage overage beyond the cap will be recorded for informational true-up only and invoiced thereafter if the parties convert to a longer-term agreement."
  b) Hard cap (no invoicing): "Redwood shall not invoice Customer for usage in excess of three (3) times the estimated Pilot consumption."

We recommend option (a) to preserve accurate usage reporting and avoid disputes; it gives Helios the protection it wants while allowing visibility for true-up.

3) Proration formula. Proposed insertion: "If the Effective Date occurs on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, charges for such partial month shall be prorated based on the number of calendar days the Pilot was active divided by the total number of days in that month (per-day proration)."

4) SKU carve-out. Suggested approach: add an appendix listing SKU IDs excluded from tier calculations. Template clause: "The Parties agree that the Product SKUs listed in Appendix A ("Excluded SKUs") shall be excluded from tiered usage calculations for the Pilot period only. Appendix A may be updated by mutual written consent."

5) Shortfall credit. We can offer a one-time credit, applied to the invoice immediately following the Pilot end date, calculated as: (Committed Monthly Fee * (1 - ActualUsage/ExpectedUsage)) * 0.5, capped at 50% of one monthly fee.

6) DocuSign and procurement: we will prepare a tracked-changes exhibit and route the Order Form via DocuSign once Helios confirms acceptance.

Internal note (Avery/Karthik): if Helios wants a larger credit or a permanent floor change, Karthik should evaluate concession impact to pricing bands. Marissa — I'm happy to convert the inline clauses to track-changes in the attached PDF.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
